extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and represented speculative-fiction authors (writers seeking publication with Tor/Forge)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and publisher expectations for authors (and their agents) aiming to publish science fiction, fantasy, and adjacent speculative work with the Tor/Forge imprints; covers editorial tastes, submission policy, commercial terms, and digital/format priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative storytelling / visionary authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge aims to publish imaginative storytelling and 'visionary authors', positioning itself as devoted to imaginative storytelling and nurturing visionary voices in speculative fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The imprint values work that demonstrates originality and imaginative scope — narratives that expand or rethink speculative concepts and voice. Examples on the list include award-winning, boundary-pushing authors; this is the cultural standard Tor/Forge seeks to uphold.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-building, character, and theme that push boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors look for projects that push the boundaries of world-building, character, and theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong submissions will show ambitious, coherent world-building, compelling character work, and thematic depth; the page explicitly cites those three elements as central to Tor's editorial identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre fit: core science fiction and fantasy (plus related genres)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary focus on science fiction and fantasy, including space opera, dystopian, hard sci-fi, epics, urban fantasy, horror, supernatural, and speculative/genre-bending works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should align with these genre areas or credibly bridge into adjacent markets; Tor/Forge cultivates a list spanning the full breadth of these genres and values both canonical and boundary-blurring works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of commercial appeal and literary quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles should balance commercial blockbusters with critically acclaimed literary works — appealing to both core genre readers and broader audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tor/Forge favors projects with crossover potential: strong sales prospects without sacrificing literary or thematic ambition. Demonstrable marketability and broader appeal are assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-caliber quality and critical recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge's list emphasizes work capable of winning major genre awards (Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, Locus) and achieving critical distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While awards are not a submission requirement, the imprint's history and selection criteria favor innovative, high-quality work that can compete for such honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series and long-term franchise potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge supports long-term series and franchise projects, exemplified by multi-book agreements for titles like The Wheel of Time, Mistborn, and The Expanse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects with potential for sustained sales, series development, and long-term career-building for authors are attractive; established franchise authors can command larger, multi-book deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author profile and sales history affect acquisition & advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance amounts vary based on author profile, sales history, and projected market performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debut authors typically receive advances in the ~$10,000–$25,000 range; established/franchise authors may command six- or seven-figure deals. Agents should set expectations according to track record and projected performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive advance and traditional royalty structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge offers competitive advances on nearly all acquired projects and follows a traditional royalty schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical royalty ranges mentioned: 10–15% on hardcover, 7–10% on trade paperback, and 25% on ebooks. The advance-plus-royalties model reflects Tor/Forge's Big Five backing and investment in authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium distribution and dedicated marketing support
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of Macmillan, Tor/Forge provides premium distribution through a global network and dedicated marketing budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors benefit from placement in major bookstores, online retailers, libraries, specialty markets, and coordinated marketing spend — factors that increase a project's commercial prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed submissions policy: agent-required
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge maintains a closed submissions policy; unsolicited manuscripts are not accepted. A literary agent must represent writers to submit directly to Tor or Forge editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Securing reputable literary representation is presented as the essential first step for authors who want to reach Tor/Forge editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scouting channels for new voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Although submissions are closed, editors and agents proactively scout new talent through industry channels like conventions, writing workshops, and contests (e.g., Writers of the Future).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspiring authors should engage in community events, contests, and workshops where editors or their agents might discover new work; these are viable discovery routes outside unsolicited queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for debut authors and author development
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge champions debut writers through programs like Tor.com Publishing and provides advances and career-building resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debut authors can access meaningful support, editorial development, and marketing resources comparable to larger publishing programs, though advance levels vary by expected market performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-first & novella-friendly imprint (Tor.com Publishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor.com Publishing is a digital-first program specializing in novellas and shorter speculative works, elevating shorter forms in the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter works and novellas are actively valued and can achieve major recognition (Hugo, Nebula, Locus); authors of shorter forms should consider Tor.com Publishing as a suitable platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital innovation and reader accessibility (DRM-free)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor was an early adopter of DRM-free ebooks, releasing its entire ebook catalog DRM-free to enhance reader accessibility and trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tor/Forge values reader accessibility and author visibility in digital formats; this history signals openness to digital-first strategies and consumer-friendly ebook policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serialized fiction and multimedia / adaptation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge emphasizes serialized fiction and multimedia storytelling and maintains a strategy that supports book-to-screen adaptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the imprint's focus on multimedia partnerships and the high rate of book-to-screen adaptations, projects with adaptation potential or transmedia possibilities may be particularly attractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in experimental formats and cross-platform storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor/Forge invests in experimental formats and cross-platform storytelling, enabling authors to expand reach across formats and platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors proposing innovative formats, serialized releases, or multimedia tie-ins should highlight those elements when appropriate, as Tor/Forge actively explores such opportunities.
